description: Expose MentorAgent as a universal AI backend from any ASP.NET Core application. Adds a SignalR hub (/mentor-hub), SSE streaming endpoint (/mentor/chat), MCP server, and A2A agent — no Blazor required.
releaseNotes:
1.0.0-rc.6

		Four defects found by running the published rc.5 packages against the sample applications - the pass rc.5's own notes implied but had not yet been done. No API change: every fix restores behaviour rc.5 already claimed.

		=== FIXED
		- BUG-068 (S3): the configuration summary was NOT written once per process, as rc.5's notes said it was. A second browser circuit still reprinted seven Information lines - the skills catalogue, the external agents, the hosted image model, the Azure image-header note, the hosted MCP server, the hosted tool list and the declarative handoff. The sentinel was claimed halfway through the build, after everything above it had already announced itself, and three collaborating builders never consulted it at all. It is now claimed first, and a later build demotes Information to Debug instead of discarding it, so an operator who turns Debug on to investigate one circuit can still see what it was built with. Degradation warnings stay per session, unchanged.
		- BUG-069 (S2): an agent supplied by an IMentorAgentSource - a declarative YAML specialist, or a host's own - joined the handoff graph and was never named in the coordinator's instructions. route_to_specialist names no agent either, so nothing the model could see said the specialist existed: asked about it, the assistant answered that there is no such agent, while the log recorded it being added to the workflow. Source-supplied agents are now listed with their descriptions beside the attribute-declared ones.
		- BUG-070 (S4): every skill on the published A2A card carried a flattened name ("Getallordersforanalysis"). The friendly-name helper splits on underscores and was being handed the PascalCase method name. That card is the one artefact whose entire audience is another machine's directory.
		- BUG-071 (S4): a turn whose input safety check met the first failure printed two stack traces instead of one - the turn's fault log was reset after that check, so its cause was recorded and immediately discarded. The reset now happens before every early return.

		1,616 tests green, build 0 warnings / 0 errors.

		1.0.0-rc.5

		Latency, cost per visitor, and the answers themselves. Measured on a live Blazor Server host before and after: time to the first character on the same question fell from 2.6-3.0 s to 1.6-2.0 s, and a shared MCP server now runs one child process for the whole application instead of one per browser circuit.

		=== NEW - options
		- ClassifierChatClient: the client MentorAgent uses for its own one-word decisions (input safety, hosted-tool scope, post-turn fact extraction). Point it at a small deployment: those calls sit in front of the reply and were measured at 707-2091 ms on gpt-4.1 for two tokens of answer. Defaults to ChatClient, and is metered under its own model id.
		- AnonymousIdentity (PerSession by default): who a signed-out visitor is, for memory and for the rate-limit counter. Every unauthenticated session used to share the literal key "anonymous", so one visitor's facts were recalled for the next and one visitor could spend everybody's allowance. BREAKING for single-user hosts that want the old behaviour: set AnonymousIdentity = Shared (MAUI, desktop, kiosk - it is what makes memory survive a restart).
		- RefuseOutOfScope (off by default): refuse a message that is not about this application, using the scope verdict the classifier already produces. Free when EnableSafetyCheck is on, because both questions now travel in one call.
		- WarmUpAtStartup (off by default): build one coordinator when the application starts, so the first visitor does not pay for the catalogue embeddings, the shared MCP sessions and the remote agent cards.
		- MentorMcpServer.Shared (null by default): one connection per process, or one per session. Unset decides by transport - a server reached over ServerUrl is shared, a server started from Command is not, because a local child process can hold state for the person who started it.
		- MapMentorAgentMcp / MapMentorAgentA2A take a configure callback, so the host can finally apply RequireAuthorization() to them. Both endpoints discarded their convention builders before this.
		- IMentorQueryEmbedding: the current message's embedding, computed once per turn. Inject it in your IMentorRagSource instead of embedding the query a second time.

		=== FASTER
		- One embedding per text instead of one per consumer. Routing, tool filtering and memory relevance were each embedding the same sentence - two to four network round trips per turn - and the tool catalogue plus the routing exemplars were re-embedded once per DI scope, i.e. once per browser circuit.
		- One classifier call instead of two: the input safety check and the hosted-tool scope check read the same message and now ask both questions in the same call.
		- The composer is handed back when the answer is complete, not after the post-turn fact extraction (a second model call, 544-767 ms measured).
		- Shared MCP sessions and a process-wide agent-card cache with a failure backoff. Two browser tabs used to mean eight node processes and 580 MB.

		=== FIXED
		- BUG-062 (S3): text written before a tool call was glued to the text after it ("...i dati.Il catalogo"), and a Markdown table opening the second response stopped being a table.
		- BUG-063 (S3): in HitlMode.Native a user without the required role was shown the confirmation banner and refused only after approving it. The role gate now runs first, as it always did in Blocking mode.
		- BUG-064 (S1): two anonymous visitors of the same site shared one memory. Now isolated per session by default, with a warning when a host opts back into the shared bucket and a second session reaches it.
		- BUG-065 (S4): the RAG "wrong scale" warning fired for thresholds on the source's own scale, once per visitor.
		- BUG-066 (S3): the hosted-tool scope classifier was built on the raw ChatClient, so its billed call appeared in no dashboard.
		- BUG-067 (S3): the safety classifier was never told what the application is equipped with, and refused three legitimate messages out of forty on a host with an MCP filesystem server and image input. It is now told, and a refused message is logged by fingerprint rather than by its text.

		=== CHANGED
		- RAG citation chips show the documents the answer actually cited. Documents are numbered in the prompt and the model is asked to cite them; if it cites none, no chips are shown.
		- MentorshipLevel.Proactive asks for one sentence before acting instead of a plan, and may only offer next steps the application can actually perform.
		- The A2A agent card publishes the application's ungated actions as skills, its input/output modes and its streaming capability. It carried a name and a description and nothing else.
		- The coordinator's configuration summary is logged once per process instead of once per session, and one provider failure produces one stack trace instead of one per component that met it.

		1,611 tests green, build 0 warnings / 0 errors.
		1.0.0-rc.4

		No change in this package. Version aligned with MentorAgent 1.0.0-rc.4, which fixes one S3 in the provider error classifier - see that package's notes. The five packages ship as a set and are meant to be upgraded together.

		1.0.0-rc.3

		One S1, and it is the reason to read these notes: every non-Blazor reference client in this package's README was unable to send a single message.

		=== FIXED - the documented React, Angular, Vue and MAUI clients could not send (S1)
		- MentorHub.SendMessage takes (string text, IReadOnlyList<MentorAttachment>? attachments = null), and its own doc-comment claimed the default let "existing 1-argument clients keep working". It does not, and cannot. SignalR binds invocation arguments positionally BY COUNT, inside the hub protocol's parser - before dispatch, before any IHubFilter, before the method body. A C# default value never reaches the wire, and hub methods cannot be overloaded, so no single signature accepts both arities.
		- invoke('SendMessage', text) is rejected with: InvalidDataException: Invocation provides 1 argument(s) but target expects 2. And because EnableDetailedErrors is off by default, what the client actually sees is "Failed to invoke 'SendMessage' due to an error on the server" - which looks like a transport or authentication problem.
		- SIX documented call sites were wrong: the JavaScript quickstart, the React hook, the Angular service, the Vue composable, the .NET MAUI / console client, and the UI-actions walk-through. Between them, every non-Blazor integration path this package advertises.
		- All six now pass the second argument, the transport table says "always send both arguments" instead of "optional trailing argument", and a warning box under the protocol reference quotes the exact exception so the next person searching for it lands somewhere useful.
		- IF YOU HAVE A CLIENT WRITTEN FROM THOSE SNIPPETS: pass null (or []) as the second argument. Nothing on the server changed - MentorAgent.Blazor's own client always sent both, which is why this survived six sample applications.

		=== SECURITY - the turn-running transports can now be protected, and warn ====
		- MapMentorAgentServer() mapped the hub and both /mentor/chat endpoints and DISCARDED their endpoint builders, so a host had no supported way to require authentication on them. The only route was to stop calling the method and re-map everything by hand. The README never mentioned authorization at all.
		- That matters because the default is not harmless. An anonymous caller can run a paid turn, and the memory key for an unauthenticated principal is the literal "anonymous" - so every anonymous caller shares ONE memory bucket, with MemoryAutoCapture (on by default) writing into it. Measured: one credential-less request stored a private code and a second, separate credential-less request read it back. RateLimitPerUser is keyed the same way, so one client exhausts everybody's allowance.
		- NEW: MapMentorAgentServer(configureTransports: e => e.RequireAuthorization()) applies a convention to the hub and both SSE endpoints. Optional - omitting it changes nothing.
		- NEW: a one-line startup warning when the SSE endpoint ends up with no authorization metadata AND memory is on. It reads the finished endpoint rather than asking whether an authentication scheme exists: plenty of applications register one and still leave this endpoint open, which is exactly the case a scheme check would miss.
		- NEW README section: every endpoint, what an anonymous caller can do with it, and how to protect it.

		=== SECURITY - /mentor/approve and /mentor/cancel are owner-only ============
		- POST /mentor/approve took an action id and approved, with no notion of who was asking: the approval store is keyed by Guid alone. Anyone who reached the server and learned an action id could approve a gated, destructive action its owner had not answered - or send approved=false to deny one they wanted, which needs no timing luck at all.
		- This is NOT new in rc.3; it predates rc.2. It shares the connection id's weakness: the documented client sends the action id in a query string, so it reaches access logs, proxy logs and browser history on the way back.
		- The Server package now records which connection raised each pending confirmation and applies the same OWNERSHIP check as /mentor/session - not merely authentication, because a signed-in stranger is still a stranger. /mentor/cancel got the same check for consistency.
		- Unchanged where there is nothing to compare: an SSE client's confirmation and an in-process Blazor Server one never pass through a hub connection, and a host with no authentication has no principal on either side.

		=== SECURITY - /mentor/session is now restricted to the connection's owner ===
		- As first written, GET /mentor/session returned the conversation to ANY caller, and POST would install a stranger's snapshot over it. Measured against a server with JWT authentication: an anonymous request received another user's transcript, 200, with the content in the body.
		- The endpoint had been written to match /mentor/approve and /mentor/cancel, and that was the wrong thing to match: those act on a turn, this one returns the conversation.
		- A SignalR connection id is 128 bits of randomness but is not a secret - it travels in a query string, so it reaches access logs, proxy logs and browser history.
		- Both verbs now check OWNERSHIP, not merely authentication: a signed-in stranger is still a stranger, which is what a plain RequireAuthorization() would have allowed. Anonymous caller against an authenticated connection is 401; a different authenticated user is 403; the owner is 200.
		- A host with NO authentication is unchanged: there is nothing to compare, and the connection id is already the only notion of "whose" such an application has.

		=== NEW - GET/POST /mentor/session (ROADMAP #34) =============================
		- A reconnect is a new connection id, therefore a new DI scope, therefore a new conversation. That is deliberate - the per-connection scope is what keeps two browsers apart - and the documented remedy has always been SerializeSessionAsync/RestoreSessionAsync. But those live on the orchestrator inside the server's scope: on WebAssembly they throw NotSupportedException, and a React, Vue or MAUI client could not reach them at all. The remedy had no transport.
		- GET /mentor/session?connectionId=... returns the snapshot, 204 when there is nothing to save (never an empty snapshot, which a client would store over a good saved conversation), 404 for an unknown connection.
		- POST /mentor/session?connectionId=... restores one, and answers 400 for a snapshot that is not MentorAgent's - without touching the live conversation.
		- HTTP rather than a hub method, for the same reason approve and cancel are.

		Otherwise the transport is unchanged: the SSE frames, the hub events and the existing endpoints are exactly as in 1.0.0-rc.2.

		=== Upgrade note - the OpenAI hold is now enforced (S1) ====================
		- rc.2 documented the hold on OpenAI 2.10.0 and asked you to keep it. That was not enough: a version in a PackageReference is a minimum, so one "dotnet add package Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI" resolved past it, built cleanly, and the process died at startup with a MissingMethodException from GetResponsesClient().
		- The core package now ships an MSBuild guard that travels to you transitively and fails the build with "error MENTOR001" if the resolved OpenAI version is 2.11.0 or later, naming the cause and the remedy. Nothing to configure; set MentorAgentSkipOpenAIVersionCheck=true only to override it deliberately.

		=== Relevant to cross-origin WebAssembly clients ==========================
		- MentorAgent.Blazor 1.0.0-rc.3 fixes an S1: before it, the WebAssembly widget could not authenticate its hub connection, so this server's identity bridge saw an anonymous caller however the client had signed the user in. If you serve a Blazor WebAssembly client, upgrade both packages together.
		- This README's authentication section now shows the C# equivalent of the JavaScript accessTokenFactory alongside it, and the JwtBearerEvents recipe that forwards ?access_token= for /mentor-hub - a WebSocket handshake cannot send an Authorization header.

		=== Verified against the published artefact ===============================
		- Driven live from a headless server with Identity on SQL Server and a cross-origin WebAssembly client: role gating in all four states (anonymous 401, no role 403, wrong role 403, right role 200), HITL approve and cancel over POST /mentor/approve, Stop over POST /mentor/cancel, and tools/list publishing 19 tools with not one gated action among them.
